topic: Assess SwiftCart delivery growth, reliability and costs.

snippets.text: SwiftCart's average cost per delivery rose from 5.00 credits in 2024 to 5.40 credits in 2025. Higher fuel and labour costs were cited in its fictional annual report.
The fictional delivery company SwiftCart completed 1 million deliveries in 2025, up from 800,000 in 2024. Its on-time delivery rate rose from 90% to 92%.
The same 2025 online grocery survey found that 360 of 600 online buyers valued delivery reliability most. The survey did not ask respondents to rank every purchasing factor.

draft_memo.title: Assessment of SwiftCart Delivery Growth, Reliability, and Costs
draft_memo.body:
SwiftCart has demonstrated notable growth in its delivery operations, completing 1 million deliveries in 2025, an increase from 800,000 in 2024 [P05]. This growth is accompanied by an improvement in its on-time delivery rate, which rose from 90% in 2024 to 92% in 2025 [P05]. These figures indicate that SwiftCart is not only expanding its delivery volume but also enhancing its reliability, a critical factor for customer satisfaction.

The average cost per delivery for SwiftCart increased from 5.00 credits in 2024 to 5.40 credits in 2025 [P06]. Higher fuel and labor costs were cited in its fictional annual report. The increase in delivery costs presents a challenge for the company, as higher fuel and labor costs were cited [P06]. This necessitates careful consideration of operational efficiencies to manage these expenses.

The 2025 online grocery survey indicated that 360 out of 600 online buyers valued delivery reliability most [P08]. However, the survey did not ask respondents to rank every purchasing factor, which limits the understanding of how delivery reliability compares to other factors influencing customer decisions. This limitation means that while reliability is valued, its relative importance remains unclear.

Additionally, there is missing data regarding customer satisfaction levels and the specific reasons behind the increased costs. Without this information, it is challenging to fully assess the implications of the cost increase on customer retention and market competitiveness. Gathering comprehensive insights into customer preferences and the factors driving operational costs would enhance the understanding of SwiftCart's position in the market.
